claim: Patchline ships role-specific tutorials for app developers, DBAs, SREs, security reviewers, and engineering managers, so each audience learns the same data-change repair loop through the evidence, commands, and handoffs it actually owns. The worker compiles structured tutorial cards from real repo fixtures and public-proof specs into one Markdown tutorial per role plus a JSON index. The gate proves all five mandated roles are present, each tutorial cites a real code or evidence path, each role has multiple concrete commands and at least three success checks, and a generic tutorial with no role or evidence is rejected.

roles.title: App developer
roles.mission: Connect application writes to migration-touched fields and decide whether generated guards or tests make the change safer to review.

real_code.proof: Django billing model with dual-write application code used by the expand/contract and staged-backfill gates.

steps: Read the application write path and identify which model field keeps legacy and new writers compatible.
Run the expand/contract template gate to see the expected invariant-backed migration sequence.
Run the staged-backfill planner gate and compare its completion proof with the generated test mutation check.
success_checks: Every tutorial decision cites the model path and at least one generated invariant or backfill artifact.
The learner can explain why tests alone are insufficient before the backfill proof passes.
A weakened generated test is rejected by the mutation gate rather than accepted as review-ready.
roles.review_decision: Request changes until generated tests cite the exact risk IDs and the backfill proof covers all pre-existing rows.
roles.handoff: Hand the DBA the table/column obligations and hand the SRE the runtime counter that proves no stale writer remains.

roles.title: DBA
roles.mission: Classify rollback feasibility, dry-run safety, and query-plan risk using engine semantics instead of SQL keyword matching.

real_code.proof: Engine-version rollback cases spanning PostgreSQL, MySQL, BigQuery, Snowflake, ClickHouse, point DML, bulk DML, and read-only controls.

steps: Inspect the engine-specific rollback case that most closely matches the proposed migration.
Run the rollback-feasibility gate and confirm the verdict distinguishes transactional, compensating, and snapshot-required changes.
Run dry-run and query-plan gates before approving production execution.
success_checks: The tutorial answer names the database engine and version that changes the verdict.
A read-only control remains unflagged while unsafe DDL or DML requires compensation evidence.
The approval notes include the required before-image, snapshot, or time-travel obligation.
roles.review_decision: Approve only after rollback feasibility, dry-run scope, and representative workload checks are all explicit.
roles.handoff: Hand app developers the required guard shape and hand SREs the lock, lag, and runtime signals to watch.

roles.title: SRE
roles.mission: Tie deploy markers, traces, logs, and incident timelines to data-change findings without overclaiming causality.

real_code.proof: OpenTelemetry collector ingestion spec with four public OTLP log fixtures from repositories not built for Patchline.

steps: Open the OTLP fixture list and identify which signals are trace, log, and SQL mutation evidence.
Run the ingestion and runtime-confidence gates to see observed impact separated from static risk.
Use the incident notebook gate to reconstruct hypotheses while preserving causality limitations.
success_checks: The tutorial output cites at least one public telemetry fixture and its pinned commit.
Runtime evidence raises or lowers confidence without deleting static proof holes.
The learner records an explicit rollback observation or missing-signal gap.
roles.review_decision: Escalate when runtime evidence supports impact or when a missing signal blocks safe rollout confidence.
roles.handoff: Hand DBAs observed lag/lock symptoms and hand engineering managers a source-free risk trend summary.

roles.title: Security reviewer
roles.mission: Keep untrusted repositories, archives, generated code, native checks, and adapter inputs isolated and auditable.

real_code.proof: Threat-model spec tied to a pinned lobsters/lobsters migration slice and adapter fixture boundaries.

steps: Read the threat-model boundaries and identify which inputs are untrusted.
Run archive, quarantine, and secret gates before allowing new fetchers, adapters, or native-check execution.
Confirm generated artifacts remain non-executable and redacted reports do not leak canary values.
success_checks: Every boundary in the threat model maps to a concrete gate or generated report artifact.
The tutorial rejects any generated code path that becomes executable by default.
The learner can identify where archive, adapter, and native-test trust boundaries differ.
roles.review_decision: Block the change until the relevant isolation, redaction, and provenance gates pass with negative controls.
roles.handoff: Hand maintainers the smallest failing boundary and the exact reproducing gate command.

roles.title: Engineering manager
roles.mission: Turn Patchline findings into staffing, review-time, fairness, and cost decisions without hiding uncertainty.

real_code.proof: Maintainer acceptance study with paired review-time observations and uncertainty-recall controls across DBA, SRE, and app-maintainer roles.

steps: Inspect paired observations and separate review-time reduction from uncertainty recall.
Run the acceptance, cost, fairness, and governance-risk gates before using Patchline output as a management metric.
Decide which role owns follow-up based on evidence, not on aggregate severity alone.
success_checks: Reported time savings preserve or improve uncertainty recall.
Cost decisions cite residual loss, manual-review thresholds, and missing evidence.
Reviewer-burden or escalation disparities are surfaced before adoption claims are made.
roles.review_decision: Adopt the workflow only when it reduces review time without increasing overconfidence or unfair escalation load.
roles.handoff: Hand role owners their next command, expected artifact, and unresolved uncertainty rather than a generic dashboard score.

success_checks: The learner says it makes sense.
